items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: And Jack comes running out of the kitchen to see what was going on.

ctx.x: So when I went, I said, "Zutty, we're going to play 'Tiger Rag'." "For what?" I said, "Because these people are jumping on my back." And we played it, and man, he was mad at me then! But what the hell, I had to get them off of me. It's his solo. I don't give a damn what he plays. That's one thing about every band I've ever had. If anybody could play anything, I'd let 'em play. You got it.

So we played that, and then we had a break. I went out to the bar. So when it comes time for the broadcast, one of the tunes we played was, you know [SNAPS FINGERS MEDIUM GROOVE], about right there. And Zutty had a solo on it, you know. And instead of him playing anything, he throws his hi-hat down and he says, DUT-DUT-DUT...you know... And Jack comes running out of the kitchen to see what was going on. It sounded like a clock ticking, you know. He played 24 bars like the blues, you know.

So I still didn't say anything. So we got to "After You've Gone," you know, and he's supposed to start it off with a drum (?), and I tried to get him to pick it up, but he wouldn't pick it up for nothing. So we went on and played that, and he played it like he was playing a waltz, soft, you know.
